clue.text: Fish supplement found in wine from Germany

indicators.note: the supplement is found inside the wine, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine
to add is to supplement

explanation.surface: A recipe for fish poached in a German white wine.
explanation.walkthrough: HOCK is the traditional British name for a Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A common North Atlantic food fish of the cod family, often smoked.

clue.text: A meeting about European question is acceptable

indicators.note: the meeting goes about, or around, the European question

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

explanation.surface: A meeting to discuss a European issue is satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Good enough or sufficient for the purpose, which is what acceptable means here.

clue.text: So-called bank needing help with no limits is nonsense

parts.note: the Dogger Bank is a large sandbank in the North Sea, and a shipping-forecast area

indicators.note: limits are the outer edges, so the word help loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A bank in need of unlimited assistance is talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called' hints that the bank is a named one, not a financial institution: Dogger Bank, a North Sea sandbank. 'with no limits' trims help to EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Badly written comic verse, and by extension any worthless rubbish or drivel.

clue.text: Abundance of work in CIA supporting company run badly

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports sits underneath, so the company and run come first
the letters of run are put together badly, that is out of order
the work is placed inside the letters of CIA

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Plenty of work at the CIA propping up a badly managed company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges RUN to RNU; OP goes 'in' CIA. 'supporting' in a down clue means the CIA part comes below.
explanation.definitionFit: The horn of plenty, a symbol of overflowing abundance, so by extension any plentiful supply.

clue.text: Carry out checks on oxygen bar

parts.note: to vet someone is to check them out
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Inspecting the oxygen supply at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is a verb: to forbid.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to forbid or block it, the power to reject a proposal.

clue.text: Go after funds to protect university

indicators.note: the funds surround the university as if guarding it

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money or funds

explanation.surface: Seeking money to keep a university safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase or follow, as when hunting quarry or seeking an aim.

clue.text: Collection points for trucks

definitions.meaning: places or times where passengers or goods are collected
light vans with an open back, in American usage

explanation.surface: Depots where lorries are collected.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both collections of goods or passengers and small open-backed vans.

clue.text: Fireplace lined with Ulster stone

indicators.note: the fireplace is lined with Ulster, so it sits inside the fireplace

parts.note: a grate is the frame holding the fire in a fireplace
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A hearth faced with stone from Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster here stands for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard igneous rock, quarried as a building stone.

clue.text: Privately owned island in clear-up after resettlement

indicators.note: the island letter goes in among the rearranged letters
resettlement means the letters of clear-up are settled again in a new order

explanation.surface: A private island being tidied after people are moved to live elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after resettlement' rearranges CLEAR-UP and I goes into the result. The definition uses the older sense of the word, 'belonging exclusively to' someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense of the word is belonging particularly to one person, as in a royal peculiar, a church owned by the monarch.

clue.text: Tramps with urge to enter drinking establishments

indicators.note: the urge goes in to the drinking establishments, so it sits inside them

parts.note: bars are places to drink
to egg on is to urge

explanation.surface: Vagrants with a craving to get into pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps and vagrants live by asking strangers for money, as mendicants do.

clue.text: Abandoned in favour of name holding advantage

indicators.note: the name is said to hold the advantage, read as N placed after it to finish the word

parts.note: being for something is being in favour of it
for someone's sake is for their benefit or advantage

explanation.surface: Deserted in preference to a name that has the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is loose here: the name does not wrap round the advantage but simply comes after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserted or left behind by everyone, a synonym for abandoned.

clue.text: Skeleton few mark or otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A sketch of a skeleton with only a few marks, or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: A basic supporting structure, like the bones of a body or the outline of a plan.

clue.text: Thirty days before gold state's capital

indicators.note: the thirty days come before the gold in the word

parts.note: June is a month of thirty days
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A month to go until gold is found in some state's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty days' points to one month in particular rather than a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of the US state of Alaska, a place founded in a gold rush.

clue.text: Short dictionary (pocket) that used to be kept by the bed

definitions.text: that used to be kept by the bed

indicators.note: short means the dictionary's name is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: Chambers is a well-known British dictionary
in snooker or billiards, to pot a ball is to pocket it

explanation.surface: A pocket-sized abridged dictionary kept on the bedside table.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is a British dictionary much used by crossword setters. The definition is a descriptive phrase: the item kept under the bed before indoor toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: Before indoor plumbing, a bowl for night-time use was kept under or beside the bed.

clue.text: Shift capital and run, getting a flyer

parts.note: to budge is to shift
Riga is the capital of Latvia
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Relocate the capital and flee, catching a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a flyer' looks like a leaflet or passenger but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small Australian parakeet, a popular cage bird that flies.

clue.text: Set out to cover unknown infection

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover the unknown by wrapping around it
out means the letters of set are put out of order

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns, so Y stands for an unknown

explanation.surface: Setting out to conceal an infection that has not been diagnosed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to STE, and 'to cover' puts Y inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small inflamed swelling on the eyelid caused by a bacterial infection of a gland.

clue.text: Person looking for understanding?

parts.note: literally someone who watches mouths moving in order to understand speech

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone seeking sympathy; in fact they look at mouths to follow what is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people often follow speech by watching the shapes the speaker's mouth makes.

clue.text: Course must include permit for game

indicators.note: the course must contain the permit, so it goes inside

parts.note: a route is a course taken
to let is to permit

explanation.surface: A golf course that must allow a particular game.
explanation.definitionFit: A casino game of chance with a spinning wheel and ball.

clue.text: Drunk cuts meal, finding wine

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of cuts meal stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunkard skips dinner and finds more wine instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fortified wine made from muscat grapes.

clue.text: Make economies? That's no good!

definitions.meaning: read as two words, this means consume a smaller amount

explanation.walkthrough: Split in two, the word is an instruction to consume less; whole, it means worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Worthless or ineffective; split in two, it means to economise by consuming less.

clue.text: House embracing a new flavour

indicators.note: the house wraps its arms around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a villa is a house

explanation.surface: A house infused with a fresh taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A flavouring from an orchid's pods, used in ice cream and cakes.

clue.text: Love to knock back drink and work

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, written as O

indicators.note: to knock back a drink is to down it; here the drink's letters are turned backwards

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone who loves downing a drink and also getting on with work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to knock back' reverses SUP, giving PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin word for a work, used for a composer's numbered compositions.

clue.text: Put up with no ale being brewed in such a system

definitions.note: the word describes a system that works on its own, not linked to others

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it

indicators.note: brewing stirs things up, so the letters of no ale are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Tolerating the lack of beer while one brews in a home set-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being brewed' rearranges NO ALE to make ALONE. The definition is the whole idea of a system that can run without connection to any other.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of a computer or device that operates independently, without needing a network.

clue.text: Make a mockery of empty double bed

indicators.note: empty means the word double is emptied of its inside, leaving just the outside letters

parts.note: a bunk is a narrow bed

explanation.surface: Mocking an unoccupied double bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To expose a claim as false or exaggerated, ridiculing it.

clue.text: Mementos of priest hoarded by Roman Catholic saint

indicators.note: the priest is stored inside the Roman Catholic abbreviation, as a hoard is kept within

parts.note: Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: Keepsakes of a priest held by a Catholic saint.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI, the biblical priest, is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Objects kept from the past as reminders, like souvenirs or keepsakes, including the remains of saints.

clue.text: Relaxed as Left must have help and support

parts.note: aid means help
to back is to support

explanation.surface: The political Left can unwind once it has assistance and backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-going and unhurried, a colloquial synonym for relaxed.

clue.text: Hearing of lines, actors may need these

indicators.note: hearing means what is heard, so the word for lines is taken by how it is said

parts.note: queues are lines of people waiting

explanation.surface: At an audition of lines, the actors need prompts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lines' tempts as a script; it is queues of people.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals in a script telling an actor when to speak or enter.

clue.text: Trouble from Italian blocking a door

indicators.note: the Italian blocks the doorway by standing inside it

parts.note: a gate is a door in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: Trouble caused by an Italian standing in the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble or disturb someone is to stir them up and make them anxious.

clue.text: A car spares outlet may have one over a barrel!

definitions.text: A car spares outlet may have one over a barrel!

parts.words: A car spares outlet may have one over a barrel!
parts.note: a motor parts shop may stock an exhaust muffler; a gun can carry a device over its barrel to quieten it

explanation.walkthrough: 'over a barrel' suggests a shop holding customers at its mercy; it is really the muzzle of a gun, and 'outlet' doubles as an exhaust outlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that muffles noise, fitted either to a car exhaust or over a gun barrel.

clue.text: Hospital worker must be tidy

definitions.meaning: an attendant who does non-medical jobs on a hospital ward

explanation.surface: A hospital attendant is required to keep things neat.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a ward attendant; the other means neatly arranged and methodical.
